case_title: Balakram v. State of Uttarakhand & Ors.
neutral_facts: The accused sought to produce certain pages of a police diary during cross-examination of a police officer. The accused obtained the diary pages under the Right to Information Act. The trial court rejected the application, stating the accused could not use the diary for cross-examination unless the police officer used it to refresh his memory or the court used it to contradict the officer. The High Court allowed the application, but the Supreme Court ultimately set aside the High Court's order, stating the accused could not use the diary for cross-examination unless the conditions under Sections 172(3) and 145 of the Evidence Act were met. The case involved an investigation into offences punishable under Sections 302 and 201 of the IPC.
